What is HTML?
HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard markup language for creating web pages. It describes the structure using elements that tell the browser how to display content.

code_examples.code:
Hello, World!

This is my first web page.

exercises.question: What does HTML stand for?
exercises.hint: Think about marking up text for hypertext.
exercises.explanation: HTML is HyperText Markup Language, the standard for web pages.

blocks.text: HTML Elements
An HTML element is defined by a start tag, content, and an end tag.

items: Void elements have no end tag

blocks.text: The Head Section
The <head> contains metadata — information about the document.

exercises.question: What goes in <head>?
exercises.explanation: <head> holds metadata like title, meta tags, links.

blocks.text: HTML Attributes
Attributes provide extra information about elements.

items: Common: href, src, alt, id, class

code_examples.code: Visit MDN

exercises.question: Where are attributes placed?
exercises.explanation: Attributes go in start tags as name='value'.

blocks.text: The Body Section
The <body> contains all visible content of the web page.
